title: Per-part stress/strain/beam CSV and motion CSV use std::fixed<<setprecision(6): strains below 5e-7 become 0.000000 and close state times merge
mechanism: writePartCSV: `ofs << std::fixed << std::setprecision(6) << point.time << "," << point.max_value << "," << point.min_value << "," << point.avg_value` (line 49-53). writeMotionCSV does the same at line 78 for Time/Avg_Disp_*/Avg_Vel_*/Avg_Acc_*/Max_Disp_Mag. With fixed(6), any value |v|<5e-7 prints as 0.000000, values around 1e-6 keep one significant digit, and times closer than 1e-6 print the same. The JSON keeps the same data at fixed(8), so the two outputs disagree.
scenario: Real production output /data/koopark/Test_Impact_A/deep_reports/Run_20260603_071717_fab346: analysis_result.json strain_history gives part 1 global_max 1.9e-07 and global_min -2.8e-07, part 12 2.3e-07, part 22 3.2e-07. strain/part_N_eff_plastic_strain.csv is 0.000000 in 992/992 rows for 22 of 24 parts. In /data/koopark/Test_hs_shell_e2e (battery deck), strain/part_30_von_mises_strain.csv is only 0.000000 or 0.000001 across all 22 states, while the JSON global_max is 9.5e-07. part_100_max_principal_strain.csv shows peak 0.000011 against the JSON's 1.066e-05. Time: the last two states 0.00500000 and 0.00500002 both print as 0.005000. In Test_Impact_A stress/part_10_von_mises.csv and motion/part_1_motion.csv, 992 rows have only 987 distinct Time values (duplicates 0.000153, 0.000658, 0.000859, 0.000960, 0.001000). Test_Postprocess_v14 has 1980 rows and 1975 distinct times. For an SI (m) deck, a max displacement of 3e-7 m prints as 0.000000.
consumers: koo_sphere_report/loader.py _load_stress_strain_csv (lines 244-265) takes true_peak/true_peak_time from these CSVs for von_mises, max/min principal stress, eff_plastic_strain, von_mises_strain and max/min principal strain. These feed the all-angle sphere report peak tables and curves. _load_motion_csv takes true_peak_g and true_peak_disp from the motion CSV. koo_impact_report/loader.py (line 1324) builds the impactor trajectory times and velocities from motion CSV. payload/analytics.py derives FFT/SRS dt from np.diff of those quantized times. koo_deep_report d3plot_reader._parse_motion_csv reads the motion curves.
suggested_fix: Write CSV numbers as significant digits, not fixed decimals (for example `std::defaultfloat << std::setprecision(10)` or `std::scientific << setprecision(9)`), as writeSurfaceStrainCSV and set-report CSVs already do. Apply this to writePartCSV, writeMotionCSV, writeSurfaceCSV, writeQualityCSV and the tensor CSV. Add a test that round-trips 3e-9 and the time pair 1.5e-7/1.4e-7.

title: NaN/Inf are written as bare nan/inf in every JSON section except hotspot_clusters, which makes the whole analysis_result.json unparseable
mechanism: timePointToJSON: `oss << std::fixed << std::setprecision(8); ... oss << "\"avg\": " << tp.avg_value` (485-490). The same raw operator<< is used in surfaceTimePointToJSON (565-591), doubleArrayToJSON (654-658), tensorToJSON (673-674), and in AnalysisTypes.hpp toExtendedJSON motion (724-726), element_quality (741-769, e.g. `", \"max_volume_change\": " << q.max_volume_change`), beam (791-796), set_reports (832) and surface_strain (865-876). iostream prints NaN as `nan`/`-nan` and infinity as `inf`, and none of these are valid JSON (Python accepts only NaN/Infinity). Only jnum() (689-699) maps non-finite values to null, and it is used only by the hotspot serializers. SinglePassAnalyzer sums element values with no isfinite filter (`stats.stress_sum += vm;`). Element-quality volume/area ratios are computed from current node coordinates with no finiteness check, and `if (!tp.volume_measured || vol_ratio > tp.volume_change_max)` accepts inf.
scenario: Reproduced by compiling the 36ea5db headers. First case: a stress point with avg_value = NaN emits `"avg": nan`, and Python json.loads fails with 'Expecting value: line 22 column 75'. Second case: an element_quality time point with volume_change_max = inf emits `"max_volume_change": inf` and the load fails. Realistic triggers: (a) a deck with erosion where freed nodes carry inf/nan coordinates, run with --element-quality. The repo itself documents that this happens in production decks: MotionAnalyzer.cpp:175-178/213-217, sphere loader.py:278-283, deep d3plot_reader.py:606-609. The hex/shell area ratio for an element touching such a node becomes inf/NaN. (b) An LS-DYNA run that error-terminates on NaN writes a final d3plot state with NaN solid stresses, so that state's avg becomes NaN. Either way one bad number makes the whole 20 MB result unreadable.
consumers: koo_deep_report/core/d3plot_reader.py _parse_outputs (449-450, `raw = json.load(f)` with no try) aborts the whole deep report. koo_sphere_report/loader.py 397-398 and koo_impact_report/loader.py 98-99 use json.load and fail the run. campaign_metrics.py 182 also uses json.loads.
suggested_fix: Route every double written into analysis_result.json through jnum() (non-finite becomes null, significant-digit formatting), including timePointToJSON, surfaceTimePointToJSON, doubleArrayToJSON, tensorToJSON and all toExtendedJSON blocks. Optionally also skip non-finite element values in SinglePassAnalyzer and in the element-quality ratios, and count them.

title: JSON histories, global_max/min, tensors and surface strain use fixed(8): strains below 5e-9 become 0 and 1e-7-scale peaks keep only 1-2 significant digits
mechanism: `oss << ind2 << "\"global_max\": " << std::fixed << std::setprecision(8) << stats.globalMax()` (512-514). timePointToJSON sets `std::fixed << std::setprecision(8)` (485). The same applies in surfaceTimePointToJSON (565), doubleArrayToJSON (654, peak_element_tensors time/sxx..szx), and AnalysisTypes.hpp:865 surface_strain_analysis (`std::setprecision(8)` on a stream already set to std::fixed at 854). The file's own jnum() comment (692-697) describes exactly this loss ('ε_p(1e-6) 는 유효숫자 3자리만 … 1e-9 는 "0.00000000"'), but the fix was applied only to hotspots.
scenario: Reproduced with the 36ea5db header: vm_strain values {3e-9, 4.9e-9, 1.234e-7, 9.53e-7} serialize as {0.0, 0.0, 1.2e-07, 9.5e-07}, and a surface-strain e1_max of 4.2e-9 becomes 0.0. Real production JSON /data/koopark/Test_hs_shell_e2e/analysis_result.json has vm_strain_history global_max 9.5e-07 and 9.3e-07, max_principal_strain 1.02e-06, and surface_strain normal_avg 1.7e-07. Test_Impact_A strain_history shows global_max 1e-08/2e-08 (1 significant digit) and part 19 `global_max 0.0` with `global_min -1e-08`, where the positive peak most likely rounded away.
consumers: koo_impact_report/loader.py 1233-1264: peak_strain = strain global_max, peak_principal_strain / min_principal_strain / peak_vm_strain = global_max/min. These go to models.py:306-308 and payload/__init__.py:132-134 (e1/evm metrics, DynaForge export keys). koo_deep_report reads PartTimeSeries global_max for KPI/peak tables and plots the data[] points. The deep report ellipsoid/Mohr views use the peak_element_tensors arrays.
suggested_fix: Serialize with jnum() (setprecision(10), defaultfloat) instead of std::fixed<<setprecision(8) for all value and time fields in partStatsToJSON, timePointToJSON, surfaceTimePointToJSON, doubleArrayToJSON, tensorToJSON and the surface_strain block.

title: element_quality per-point data[] drops the aspect/volume/skew/warp measured flags, so the deep report plots AR=0 and volume ratio=1.0 for unmeasured parts
mechanism: `extra << "{\"time\": " ... << ", \"ar_max\": " << tp.aspect_ratio_max << ", \"ar_avg\": " << tp.aspect_ratio_avg << ", \"jac_measured\": " ... << ", \"skew_max\": " << tp.skewness_max << ", \"warp_max\": " << tp.warpage_max << ", \"vol_min\": " << tp.volume_change_min << ", \"vol_max\": " << tp.volume_change_max` (758-770). Only jac_measured is written per point. ElementQualityTimePoint has aspect_measured/volume_measured/skewness_measured/warpage_measured, but they are not serialized, so the defaults (aspect 0.0, volume 1.0, skew/warp 0.0) go out as values. writeQualityCSV correctly leaves these cells blank.
scenario: Reproduced: a solid part whose elements are all tets stored as degenerate hex8 (common in drop models) has computeAspectRatio8 fail on its zero-length edge and distinct8=false. The per-point JSON is then {ar_max: 0.0, ar_avg: 0.0, vol_min: 1.0, vol_max: 1.0, skew_max: 0.0, warp_max: 0.0}, while the part-level aspect_measured=false and volume_measured=false. A tria-only shell part likewise gets skew_max/warp_max 0.0 at every state.
consumers: koo_deep_report/report/html_report.py initQualityCharts (2011-2040) plots q.data.map(d=>d.ar_max / ar_avg / vol_min / vol_max / warp_max / skew_max) with no flag check. The user sees a flat AR=0 curve and a flat 'Volume/Area Change = 1.0' (no deformation) curve for tet parts, even though the summary table above correctly shows '—'. Reachable in deep report runs with --element-quality.
suggested_fix: Serialize ar_measured/vol_measured/skew_measured/warp_measured per point (or write null via jnum when unmeasured) and have the charts skip unmeasured points.

title: Time column of stress/strain/motion CSVs written with std::fixed setprecision(6): µs-resolution times are quantized, duplicated, or collapse
mechanism: writePartCSV:49 `ofs << std::fixed << std::setprecision(6) << point.time`. writeMotionCSV:78 does the same, as do writeSurfaceCSV:117 and writeQualityCSV:246. With time in seconds, every stamp is rounded to 1 µs. The JSON writer uses 8 decimals and writeSurfaceStrainCSV uses scientific notation, so only these CSVs lose it.
scenario: All 28 production result sets I surveyed use output intervals of about 1.008e-6 s. In /data/koopark/Test_Impact_A/deep_reports/Run_20260603_071717_fab346/motion/part_17_motion.csv the true times 3.02e-6 and 5.05e-6 are written as 0.000003 and 0.000005. Five stamps are duplicated (0.000153, 0.000658, 0.000859, 0.00096, 0.001), and consecutive diffs take only the values {0, 1e-6, 2e-6}. For Δt spanning 1/2/3 output steps the CSV-derived Δt error reaches 98%/49%/32%. For a deck with 1e-7 s output, 10001 states collapse to 1001 distinct stamps, a peak at 1.5e-7 is written as 0.000000, and the impact FFT estimates fs = 1e6 Hz instead of 1e7 Hz, reporting a 5 kHz dominant mode as 500 Hz (reproduced numerically).
consumers: koo_impact_report loader.py:1141 pm.times becomes t_peak_g (s4_part_g table in ms with 3 decimals) and traj.t_first_contact (loader.py:422). physics.py:96 wave speed r/(t_peak−t_first) uses Δt of a few µs, and part of the 'Δt 해상도 부족' divergence its 12000 m/s ceiling guards against comes from this. analytics.py FFT (fs from diff(t)) and SRS (dt=median diff, np.interp on non-increasing t) are also affected. koo_sphere_report loader.py:254/294 uses these times for true_peak_time and plots. koo_deep_report d3plot_reader.py:602 uses them for motion plots.
suggested_fix: Write the time column with std::scientific (or defaultfloat) and setprecision(10) in all four writers, matching writeSurfaceStrainCSV. Bump UA_OUTPUT_SCHEMA so existing CSVs are regenerated.

title: --skip-existing treats bare existence of analysis_result.json as 'completed'
mechanism: `bool isAnalysisCompleted(const fs::path& result_dir) { return fs::exists(result_dir / "analysis_result.json"); }` is used at :763. The JSON is written inside exportResults (:526-531) before render jobs, section views and saveAnalysisMetadata (:672-700). There is no check on analyzer version, config, or d3plot mtime.
scenario: analyze_and_report.sh (host tool kept by deploy_from_sif.sh) runs `--recursive output --output analysis_results --skip-existing` by default. (1) Analyzer upgraded, e.g. the 08-11 displacement fix: every existing Run is skipped, and the sphere report keeps 19× displacement for old runs next to corrected new runs. (2) The section-view pass reads all states and is OOM-killed after the JSON was written: next invocation prints 'Skipped (already analyzed)' and the run never gets renders. (3) A deck is re-simulated in place: the old results are kept.
consumers: koo_sphere_report via analysis_results/, deep render gallery
suggested_fix: Write a completion marker last (after renders and metadata), carrying tool_commit and a config hash. Compare that marker and the d3plot mtime in isAnalysisCompleted. Write the JSON atomically (tmp + rename).

title: Custom-report run into the documented shared folder overwrites deep's analysis_result.json, wiping motion_analysis / element_quality / hotspot_clusters
mechanism: exportResults writes `output_dir + "/analysis_result.json"` unconditionally whenever output_json is set. koo_custom_report runner.py:155 always emits `json: true` with the user's -o directory. __main__.py:21-22 documents `-o Run_*/Output/report` as the KooChainRun convention, which is the same folder where deep writes analysis_result.json and which sphere_report.sh symlinks and impact loader.py:1942 reuses. A set_reports-only run has no motion, quality or hotspot jobs, so those arrays are serialized empty.
scenario: Reproduced with the built binary on /data/ball_drop_test_v7/ex01_prony_2term_ref. A deep-style run into report/ gave motion_analysis [1,2,3]. Running the exact YAML from runner.build_ua_yaml (part set, parts [2]) into the same folder rewrote analysis_result.json with motion_analysis []. Any hotspot_clusters or element_quality from a deep run with --hotspot-clusters/--element-quality become [] too. The motion CSVs remain, so the impact _reuse check still passes and silently takes the stripped JSON.
consumers: koo_sphere_report hotspot section (_collect_hotspot_clusters returns [] as if never run), koo_impact_report/_parse_outputs (hotspot_clusters, element_quality), koo_deep_report campaign_metrics, federate/scatter reading Output/report
suggested_fix: Have koo_custom_report pass `json: false` (it only reads metrics.json) or use a subfolder. Alternatively, have the C++ side merge into or refuse to overwrite an existing analysis_result.json from a different job set.

title: Recursive result folder name: symlinked runs escape the output root, and 'case 1' / 'case_1' collide
mechanism: `fs::path rel_path = fs::relative(canonical_dir, canonical_root);` keeps '/' and '..'. The `while (... substr(0,3) == ".._")` cleanup is dead since '/' is no longer replaced, and `c == ' ' -> '_'` maps distinct names to one folder. Then `result_dir = output_root / folder_name` (:757).
scenario: Reproduced by compiling the exact functions. root/output/Run_A is a symlink to elsewhere/sims/Run_A, and the result goes to <root>/elsewhere/sims/Run_A (inside the simulation tree), not analysis_results/Run_A. The sphere loader finds no analysis_results/Run_A/analysis_result.json, `return None` drops it silently, and the run disappears from the all-angle report. 'output/case 1' and 'output/case_1' both map to analysis_results/case_1: the second overwrites the first, or under --skip-existing is skipped and reported with the first case's data.
suggested_fix: Build names from the non-canonical path relative to root, or reject/encode '..' components. Make the name injective (escape '_' or keep spaces), and detect duplicate result_dir before running.

title: findD3plotDirectories returns a partial list on a scan error and the batch still reports success
mechanism: `catch (const std::exception& e) { std::cerr << "Error scanning directories: " ...; }` followed by `return result;`. runRecursiveAnalysis prints 'Found N', 'Total: N' and returns 0 if those succeed. With follow_directory_symlink a symlink cycle throws midway.
scenario: Reproduced: output/Run_1, Run_2 and Run_3 each contain d3plot, plus Run_2/parent_link -> '..'. The scan throws 'Too many levels of symbolic links'. The returned list holds 41 entries, all Run_1 via the loop, and zero entries for Run_2 or Run_3. Exit code is 0, and the sphere report is built without Run_2 and Run_3.
suggested_fix: Use error_code iteration and skip only the failing entry, dedupe by canonical path, and exit non-zero (or list skipped subtrees) when the scan is incomplete.

title: NARBS user-ID arrays read in the wrong order: shell, thick-shell and beam element IDs are shifted
mechanism: The parser reads the ID blocks as nodes, solids, `// 3. Thick shell element IDs (NSORTT = NELT)` (l.79), `// 4. Beam element IDs` (l.91), `// 5. Shell element IDs` (l.103). The spec it cites (ls-dyna_database.txt l.728-732) gives the order NUSERN, NUSERH, NUSERB (beams), NUSERS (shells), NUSERT (thick shells). The NARBS header pointers agree with the spec: NSRB=NSRH+NEL8, NSRS=NSRB+NEL2, NSRT=NSRS+NEL4. GeometryParser::parse_narbs then copies these IDs into mesh.real_shell_ids / real_thick_shell_ids / real_beam_ids and into shells[i].id / thick_shells[i].id / beams[i].id.
scenario: Real deck /data/battery_study/case_01_phase1_stacked_tier-1/d3plot has NARBS=23091, NEL4=7370, NELT=4704, and header pointers [-1, 9739, 10900, 10900, 18270, ...] (NSRT=18270=NSRS+NEL4). Reading it the parser's way assigns thick shells the IDs [393..8232], which are really shell IDs. Shells get [8233..10624], which is a mix of real shell and thick-shell IDs. Lasso and the spec give shells [393..12074] and thick shells [1..10624]. None of the 7370 shell IDs match. The same shift hits any deck with NARBS>0 and NELT>0 that also has shells or beams.
consumers: Hotspot clusters for element_type shell/thick_shell take peak_element_id from mesh.real_shell_ids / real_thick_shell_ids (HotspotClusterAnalyzer.cpp:608-610, 870-872). That ID goes to analysis_result.json, then the koo_deep_report HTML hotspot table (html_report.py:2264) and the campaign_cli elout cross-check (campaign_cli.py:254, which compares by user element ID, so it checks the wrong elements). Element-quality worst_*_elem for shell/tshell parts (UnifiedAnalyzer.cpp:1697,1766 → quality CSV). BeamAnalyzer max/min_element_id when NELT>0 (BeamAnalyzer.cpp:112).
suggested_fix: Read the ID blocks in spec order: nodes, solids, beams, shells, thick shells. Better still, seek to each block with the header pointers (NSRH/NSRB/NSRS/NSRT). Add a regression test on a deck that has both shells and thick shells, and check the IDs against lasso.

title: Exterior-face detection breaks on tets stored as degenerate hex8: interior tets land in the ±Z surface results and real boundary faces are missed
mechanism: Each solid contributes 6 hex faces from HEXA_FACE_NODES, keyed by `generateFaceHash(face_nodes)` over the sorted 4 node indices, and `if (pair.second == 1)` marks a face exterior. LS-DYNA stores a tet as (A,B,C,D,D,D,D,D). Face 0 {0,3,2,1} then becomes the 4-node set {A,B,C,D}, which is unique to that element, so it always counts once and is always 'exterior'. The real faces ABC and ACD never appear as their own hash, so faces shared between tets never cancel. These faces have non-zero normals, so the zero-normal filter added in 36ea5db does not remove them.
scenario: I replicated the algorithm exactly in Python on a 2x2x2 cube split into 48 Kuhn tets in (a,b,c,d,d,d,d,d) form. The true boundary has 48 triangles. The algorithm returns 144 'exterior' faces with non-zero normals, and 120 of them are interior. The +Z 45° filter picks 16 faces, 8 of them interior (elements 4,5,16,17,28,29,40,41). Surface von Mises max/avg for 'Top (+Z)' and 'Bottom (-Z)' therefore include interior elements, and boundary tets whose only outer face is ABC or ACD are dropped. The code's own comment notes MinimumModel.k is 76% tets.
consumers: surface_defaults injects the ±Z SURFACE_STRESS/SURFACE_STRAIN jobs into every unified_analyzer run (UnifiedAnalyzer.cpp:135-155). Results go to surface/*_stress.csv, surface/*_strain.csv, analysis_result.json surface_analysis and surface_strain_analysis. Users read these raw outputs; the ±Z investigation behind 36ea5db started from them.
suggested_fix: Build faces from each element's unique-node topology (tet: 4 triangles, wedge: 2 triangles + 3 quads, pyramid, hex). Hash triangles by their 3 sorted unique nodes. Drop faces with fewer than 3 unique nodes before counting.

title: Element quality looks at only 10 evenly spaced states, so transient inversions and peak distortion are missed
mechanism: `size_t n_samples = std::min(n_states, size_t(10));` ... `size_t idx = i * (n_states - 1) / (n_samples - 1);`. Only those states are analyzed. ElementQualityStats::computeGlobalStats then reports min_jacobian, max_negative_jacobian_count, min/max_volume_change and peak_aspect_ratio as extremes 'across all time'.
scenario: A 992-state drop test is sampled at states 0,110,220,...,991. An element that inverts (scaled Jacobian < 0) only during states 130-170 of the impact is never evaluated. The output is max_negative_jacobian_count=0 and a min_jacobian from a calm state, and the report prints '음수Jac=0개'.
consumers: analysis_result.json element_quality → koo_deep_report d3plot_reader.py:491 → the console summary AR/Jac/음수Jac (__main__.py:1399-1411) and the report. Also quality/part_*_quality.csv. Enabled by koo_deep_report --element-quality.
suggested_fix: Evaluate every state, or at least track per-element extremes over all states (the states are already in memory). If sampling stays, record the sampled state count in the JSON and do not call the result a peak.

title: Segment-set parent-element lookup sends connectivity values (internal 1-based indices) through the user-node-ID map
mechanism: `auto ridx = [&](int32_t nid) { ... nid2idx.find(nid) ... }` where nid2idx maps real_node_ids to index. The map is correct for segment nodes (user IDs), but it is also applied to `for (int32_t nid : mesh.solids[ei].node_ids) { const int32_t ni = ridx(nid); if (ni >= 0) node2elem[ni].push_back(ei); }`. Solid connectivity holds internal 1-based indices; the NodeIndexResolver comment in the same file (l.891-913) says the only correct conversion is nodes[nid-1].
scenario: I replicated the logic in Python. Node user IDs are {1..100, 151..250}, i.e. internal 1..200 with a gap. A segment on the bottom face of element 30 (user nodes 175,179,180,176) resolves to parent element 42 instead of 30. Element 3, in the identity range, still resolves correctly. With non-overlapping offsets (e.g. part nodes starting at 100001) the connectivity lookups simply miss: segments are dropped with the misleading note '셸 면이거나 절점 미존재', and set metrics come from a subset or are not computed.
consumers: set_reports/<name>/metrics.json and von_mises.csv / eff_plastic_strain.csv for set_type=segment (computeDirectSetMetrics l.1418-1469), plus the parent part candidates used for set views → koo_custom_report html_report.py (peak, peak_element_id).
suggested_fix: Build node2elem with `ni = nid - 1` (internal index, range-checked). Keep ridx only for the segment's user node IDs.

title: Deleted (eroded) elements enter all per-part and surface statistics as real zeros; StateData::deleted_solids is parsed but never read
mechanism: StateDataParser::parse_deletion_data fills state.deleted_solids/deleted_shells for MDLOPT=2. No analyzer reads them; a grep finds only NodalAverager. analyzePartStatsSequential loops `for (size_t elem_idx = 0; elem_idx < num_solid_elements_; ++elem_idx)` and folds every element into stress_min/avg, principal min/max and strain_min/avg. SurfaceStressAnalyzer, SurfaceStrainAnalyzer, clusterTimeAggregate and processElementQualityJobs have the same gap.
scenario: In the real erosion deck /data/koopark/Test_DTMIN_erode/dtmin_0p1 (MAXINT=-10003 → MDLOPT=2), last state in d3plot21 at t=5.0e-4, the deletion table marks 6 solids as deleted. All 7 words of each deleted element (6 stresses + eps) are exactly 0.0. The part's Min_von_mises becomes 0.000000 with Min_Element_ID set to an eroded element, and averages drop as more elements erode. The hotspot mean_timemax cluster mean after erosion and element-quality negative-Jacobian counts (eroded elements keep moving nodes) are contaminated in the same way.
consumers: stress/part_*_von_mises.csv and principal/strain CSVs (Min_/Avg_ columns) → koo_sphere_report min_values/avg_values (loader.py:230-270). JSON avg_vals plotted in koo_deep_report. surface/*.csv. hotspot mean_timemax. element_quality counts.
suggested_fix: Build a per-state deleted mask from state.deleted_solids (1-based array order) and skip those elements in min/avg/count, surface faces, cluster means and quality. Emit a per-state deleted-element count so consumers can see erosion.

title: All part, motion, surface and quality CSVs are written with std::fixed setprecision(6); fine time steps and small strains/displacements collapse
mechanism: writePartCSV: `ofs << std::fixed << std::setprecision(6) << point.time << "," << point.max_value ...` (l.49). writeMotionCSV (l.78), writeSurfaceCSV (l.117) and writeQualityCSV time (l.246) do the same. Only the surface-strain CSV uses scientific.
scenario: For time in seconds, 2.5e-6 and 3.5e-6 both print as '0.000003', and 1.0e-7, 1.4e-7, 1.5e-7, 2e-7, 3e-7 and 4e-7 all print as '0.000000' (checked with %.6f). With output intervals of 1e-7..1e-6 s the Time column has duplicate or zero rows. Eff. plastic strain 4.4e-7 → '0.000000'. A principal/vm strain of 3e-9 → '0.000000'. GPa stress 3.2e-5 → '0.000032' (2 significant digits). SI-deck displacement 2e-7 m → '0.000000'.
consumers: koo_sphere_report loader reads stress/strain/motion CSVs and computes true_peak/true_peak_time from these strings (loader.py:230-320, 423-452). koo_impact_report builds the impactor trajectory times/velocities from the motion CSV (loader.py:1323-1346) and interpolates matsum KE on those times. koo_deep_report motion CSV parser (d3plot_reader.py:577-615).
suggested_fix: Write with std::scientific or std::defaultfloat and setprecision(9) (max_digits10 for float data), as the set-report CSVs already do.

title: Part-name lookup reads an arbitrary .k file, ignores *INCLUDE and *PART_ variants; a zero-match part_pattern on surface jobs turns into the whole model
mechanism: findKeywordFile falls back to the first `fs::directory_iterator(dir)` entry with a .k/.key/.dyn extension. parsePartNamesFromKeyword does not follow *INCLUDE, skips any line containing "*PART_" (l.48: *PART_COMPOSITE, *PART_CONTACT, *PART_INERTIA), and stops after the first PID card. filterPartsByPattern then silently falls back to 'Part_N' names. In processSurfaceStressJobs/processSurfaceStrainJobs, `std::vector<int32_t> target_parts = job.part_ids;` stays empty when the pattern matches nothing, and `extractSolidExteriorSurfaces(target_parts)` with an empty list means all parts.
scenario: In /data/battery_study/case_01_phase1_stacked_tier-1 the readdir order returns 07_control_phase1.k first. That file has no *PART; the 34 *PART cards are in 02_mesh_stacked_tier-1.k, pulled in by *INCLUDE from 01_main. Every name pattern matches nothing. A surface_stress job {name: 'PCB bottom', part_pattern: 'PCB*', direction -Z} then reports the -Z surface of the whole model under the name 'PCB bottom'. In koo_custom_report set_reports, a pattern that matches only some parts (others defined via *PART_COMPOSITE or in includes) silently covers a subset; a note is added only when nothing matches.
consumers: surface/<job>_stress.csv / _strain.csv and analysis_result.json surface_analysis. koo_custom_report set metrics (resolved_parts, peaks). Render part_pattern selection. part_pattern analysis jobs can be written from the koo_deep_report GUI (gui/app.py:139).
suggested_fix: Resolve names from the main deck, following *INCLUDE, and accept *PART_* variants and multi-part *PART blocks. Treat a non-empty pattern that matches 0 parts as an error or a skipped job, never as 'all parts'.
